unit.title: Digital accessibility in France
unit.description: European Accessibility Act since June 2025, who is covered, RGAA and WCAG, alt text, contrast, keyboard, forms, captions, controls and sanctions

cards.definition: EU directive 2019/882, applied since 28 June 2025: e-commerce sites and apps, banking, transport ticketing, e-books, audiovisual media and some devices sold to consumers must be accessible to people with disabilities. Existing e-commerce sites are covered too.
cards.example: An online shop must let a blind customer find a product, add it to the cart and pay with a screen reader.

cards.definition: Service providers with fewer than 10 employees and no more than 2 million euros of turnover or balance sheet are exempt for services. Others can invoke a disproportionate burden only with a documented assessment.
cards.example: A 4-person online shop is exempt; a 30-person one is not.

cards.definition: WCAG are the international accessibility guidelines (level AA is the usual target). The RGAA is the French reference framework based on them, with criteria and tests.
cards.example: An audit against the RGAA checks 106 criteria such as alternative texts, contrast and keyboard navigation.

cards.definition: Text describing an informative image for screen readers, in the alt attribute. Decorative images get an empty alt so they are skipped. A product photo needs a useful description.
cards.example: alt="Navy wool coat, knee length, with a hood" instead of alt="image1".

cards.definition: Text must stand out from its background: at least 4.5 to 1 for normal text under WCAG AA (3 to 1 for large text). Light grey on white often fails.
cards.example: A pale grey promo price on a white page is hard to read for many people.

cards.definition: Everything must work without a mouse: tab through links, buttons and fields in a logical order, with a visible focus. Many users of assistive tools navigate by keyboard.
cards.example: A cookie banner that cannot be closed with the keyboard blocks the whole site.

cards.definition: In France the DGCCRF checks e-commerce accessibility, with other regulators for their sectors, and courts can order fixes: in June 2026 a court ordered Carrefour to make its site and app accessible within six months.
cards.example: Associations of disabled people can also take legal action.

exercises.prompt: Since when does the European Accessibility Act apply to e-commerce?
choices: 28 June 2025
1 January 2020
27 September 2026
It applies only to public sites
exercises.explain: Since 28 June 2025, consumer e-commerce services must meet accessibility requirements, existing sites included.

exercises.prompt: Which online shop is exempt for its services?
choices: One with 6 employees and 1.5 million euros of turnover
One with 40 employees and 8 million euros
Any shop founded before 2025
Any shop selling only clothes
exercises.explain: Micro-enterprises (under 10 staff and up to 2 million euros) are exempt for services.

choices: The French accessibility reference framework based on WCAG
A French law about cookie banners on sites
A label given to low-carbon websites
The French rules for prices shown online
exercises.explain: The RGAA turns WCAG into testable criteria used in French audits.

exercises.prompt: Which alt text is best for a product photo?
choices: Navy wool coat, knee length, with a hood
image1.jpg, the original file name
Photo of a product
Best coat ever, buy it now
exercises.explain: Describe what a sighted user learns from the image. Keywords stuffing and file names do not help.

exercises.prompt: What alt should a purely decorative background image have?
choices: An empty alt, alt=""
A long description of the pattern
The name of the brand
No alt attribute and a title instead
exercises.explain: Empty alt tells screen readers to skip it.

exercises.prompt: What minimum contrast does WCAG AA require for normal text?
choices: 2 to 1
10 to 1
exercises.explain: Large text needs 3 to 1. Check with a contrast tool before validating a design.

exercises.prompt: A site is accessible if it looks fine with a mouse on a big screen.
exercises.explain: False. Keyboard use, screen readers, zoom and captions must all work. Test with the keyboard only.

exercises.prompt: Your cookie banner cannot be closed with the keyboard. Why is it serious?
choices: It blocks keyboard users from the whole site
It only changes the colour of the banner
It improves conversion for everyone
It is a minor SEO detail
exercises.explain: One blocking element can make the entire service unusable, which is exactly what controls look for.

exercises.prompt: Which video practice helps deaf and hard of hearing users?
choices: Captions synchronised with the sound
Autoplay with the sound turned on
Background music only, no voice
A smaller video player on mobile
exercises.explain: Captions also help everyone watching without sound, which is most social video viewing.

exercises.title: An accessibility check on a fashion site
exercises.scenario: A 60-person fashion e-commerce company asks whether it must act on accessibility.

steps.prompt: Is it covered by the European Accessibility Act?
choices: Yes: consumer e-commerce, and it is not a micro-enterprise
No: only public websites are covered
No: fashion is exempt from the rules
Only for its physical shops, not online
steps.feedback: E-commerce services to consumers are covered since June 2025; the micro-enterprise exemption does not apply.

choices: An audit against RGAA criteria on key journeys: search, cart, payment
Installing an overlay widget that promises compliance
Rewriting the brand guidelines
Waiting for a control to see what fails
steps.feedback: Overlay widgets do not make a site compliant. Audit the real journeys and fix the code.

steps.prompt: Which fixes usually bring the biggest gains fast?
choices: Form labels, alt texts, contrast and keyboard access
New product photos in higher resolution
A faster homepage carousel
More pop-ups with offers
steps.feedback: These basics block the most users and are often cheap to fix.

exercises.explain: Accessibility is now a legal duty for most e-commerce, and a better experience for everyone.
